summary: Jordan Avery, founder of Avery Freight Analytics, meets Dan Ellison, Northwind's COO, with Theo Lindqvist and Ines Carvalho, to win the ABC contract: twelve months of network-planning and terminal-consolidation analytics across 31 warehouses and the nine terminals that came with Tailspin Freight. Northwind paid for one network study in 2024 and shelved it. Win by showing a model their own two analysts keep current, priced on Ines's definition of cost per shipment. Dan approves; the CFO signs.

deadlines.title: Written proposal to Theo, 6 pages max
Pricing sheet on Ines's cost-per-shipment basis

matters.title: They already paid for one network study and shelved it.
matters.text: A large consulting firm ran a network review in 2024; it never reached operations. Win by showing a model Theo's two analysts keep current every month.

matters.title: Dan Ellison approves, and he judges on a number first.
matters.text: Then what breaks if you are wrong, then the first step. Bring one number, one named risk and a 90-day plan. Do not offer a menu of options.

matters.title: Ines Carvalho owns cost per shipment, and it is defined two ways.
matters.text: Northwind and Tailspin count it differently. The business case and the pricing sheet must use her definition, or the deal stalls at terms.

drives.label: Financial
drives.line: Margin from the Tailspin overlap before the fund sells.

drives.label: Social
drives.line: A family carrier that still wants to look like one.

drives.label: Commercial
drives.line: Density, service, cost per shipment, in that order.

drives.label: Technical
drives.line: One TMS by June, and a network model their own people run.

people.name: Dan Ellison
people.title: Chief Operating Officer
people.judges: A number first, then what breaks if you are wrong, then the first step. Hedging marks you down.

verdict.line: Delivers. Ran network design at a 3PL and then a larger carrier for twelve years; the Tailspin integration is on schedule.

people.drives: Margin from the Tailspin overlap inside the fund's hold, and one name next to every decision.
people.family: Married, two children. Lives in Chicago, Lincoln Park area.

drivers.label: Financial
drivers.line: Paid on the exit, so the Tailspin margin is his number.

drivers.label: Social
drivers.line: Standing among operators, at the club and at the summit.

drivers.label: Commercial
drivers.line: Every building has to earn its place.

drivers.label: Technical
drivers.line: A model with one name next to every decision.

people.name: Theo Lindqvist
people.title: VP Network and Engineering
people.judges: Whether the model stays alive with his two analysts after we leave, and whether operations will trust it.

verdict.line: Keeps models alive. His two analysts ran Northwind's network studies for three years before 2024, and still refresh them.

people.drives: A model his team owns, and no surprises for operations.
people.family: Married. Lives in the Oak Park area.

people.name: Ines Carvalho
people.title: Director, FP&A
people.judges: Whether cost per shipment is defined the way she defines it, and whether the price traces to it.

verdict.line: Strong on numbers, thin in public. Two integration models at a prior carrier are on her profile; neither can be checked from outside.

people.drives: One definition of cost per shipment across both companies, and a price she can trace.
people.family: No public family information found. Lives in the Chicago area.
